title: BackgroundCooks
content:
A Cooking Garden
BackgroundCooks was my first Digital Garden and is meant as a recipe book.
In it I break down recipes into multiple ones whenever a part could be used for more than one recipe. For instance I have a Pie Crust recipe that I use for multiple other recipes and so they just link to the pie crust recipe for that section.
Some recipes I have created from scratch such as my Basic Sourdough and others that I have re-written for my own understanding and ease of reading from other sources, with those sources cited like with Vedbread a recipe from Hero's Feast: A D&D Cookbook.
I update it periodically whenever I get into a new recipe, but that recipe usually goes through several revisions before I publish it.

title: Home Server
content:
Why a Home Server?
It started with wanting to stop using google/microsoft for things like backing up photos, contacts, documents, ect. I considered using a service like Proton where it's hosted in a famously neutral country, but decided that for the long run, I'd rather just have all the data in a box at home.
Frankly, I wanted more say of what is done with my data existing online. Now I'm more selective with what I share online and everything else gets backed up to NextCloud and Jellyfin.
Hardware
Motherboard: Raspberry Pi 4 8GB
Case: Argon EON Pi NAS
Storage: 1x1TB SSD, 1x4TB HDD
Software
OS: Raspberry Pi OS (latest)
Management Software: Open Media Vault 7
Docker Containers:

PiHole - DHCP server, network wide adblocking
NginxProxyManager - GUI frontend for Nginx, used for reverse proxy
Jellyfin - A media server for personal use
NextCloud - A cloud similar to office365 or google
Actual Budget - A budgeting software similar to YNAB

title: garden.backgroundlogic.dev
content:
About
I made this 'Garden' as a place to share things I make and to have a place to point people to when they ask. This website is hosted on GitHub using the GitHub Pages feature, it is a static site built using Obsidian Notes with an addon called Digital Garden.
How?
While obsidian notes is primarily a note taking application that functions like a wiki, digital garden uploads selected notes to a GitHub repository with a static site template, then updates GitHub Pages. Once setup the workflow is very simple, just write a note, check the box to publish, and push the notes to GitHub. After a minute the website updates with the new changes.
